chunks: And to Solomon (We subjected) the tempestuous wind which blew swiftly at his bidding to the land which We had blessed; and We are cognisant of everything.
ai.seo_question: What specific natural force was subjected to Solomon's command according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores Solomon’s unique status among prophets by linking his control over the 'strong wind' (al-Rih al-'Asif) to his divine mission of establishing justice and building the Temple. The reference to the 'blessed land' is often interpreted not only geographically as Jerusalem but also spiritually as the realm of prophetic authority, while the concluding phrase emphasizes God’s omnipresence in all aspects of creation.
